entries.subject: DAMIT 5926: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-5926.txt. Model 5926, version 2021-11-12, pole (74°, 63°), period 6.041319 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 218 ±3 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Other DAMIT shape solutions
entries.finding: The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 149: pole (72°, 60°), 6.04131 h, version 2011-03-26, archive diameter 204 km; 1821: pole (81°, 67°), 6.041321 h, version 2017-06-13, archive diameter 220 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent shape, spin or scale evidence distinguishes these alternatives, or a changed release offers a demonstrably better supported model.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 30 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 1817 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.14 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.75; 2 of 30 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists. Checked 2026-09-18 for the published-comparison route, which reads a release record against the survey’s own Table A.1 pole. The table prints Thisbe’s pole as (350°, 116°), past the pole: the direction (170°, 64°), which gives the 21° obliquity the table also prints. The release record reads (74.0°, 62.8°), as DAMIT model 5926 states, and its two column orders lie 34.1° and 38.9° from the table’s pole. The record and the table describe different solutions, so the setup refuses it, as it does Eleonora’s and Nemesis’s.
entries.revisitWhen: A registration reference for this body: a spacecraft map, or frames in which the cross-frame test resolves markings (peak correlation above 0.15 with a mirror margin above 1.5 on most frames).
